reason: The hypothesis relies on two key premises: edge dislocation dominance and their wavy motion in random alloys. E1 supports edge dislocation dominance in a specific refractory HEA (NbTaTiV), and E2 supports the wavy motion and strength control by edge dislocations in random BCC alloys. However, the crucial premises linking coherent nanoprecipitates to controlled edge dislocation motion, enhanced strain hardening, and crack-tip blunting are not supported by the cited evidence, which does not discuss nanoprecipitates or their effects on toughness.
premises: Edge dislocations dominate plastic deformation in some refractory high-entropy alloys, unlike conventional BCC metals.
Edge dislocations in random BCC alloys adopt a wavy morphology due to local solute fluctuations, controlling strength.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can impede and regulate edge dislocation motion.
Controlled edge dislocation motion by nanoprecipitates enhances strain hardening and crack-tip blunting.
This mechanism simultaneously improves high-temperature strength retention and fracture toughness.
